atoms.text: This guide configures the ApiGate service to deliver HTTP access log files to the S3 bucket example-gateway-logs in account 111122223333. ApiGate assumes the IAM role ApiGateLogDelivery and writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under the prefix gateway/access/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not modified. In the IAM console, open the role and add an inline policy that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-gateway-logs/gateway/access/*. Do not add or edit any bucket policy statement for this role, and leave Block Public Access enabled on the bucket. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, the identity-based allow is sufficient unless an explicit deny applies. In the ApiGate delivery settings, enter the bucket name, the prefix, and the role ARN. Use the Send test file action and confirm that a test object appears under the prefix. If delivery fails with AccessDenied, check the resource ARN in the inline policy for a mistyped prefix.

This guide configures the ApiGate service to deliver HTTP access log files to the S3 bucket example-gateway-logs in account 111122223333. ApiGate assumes the IAM role ApiGateLogDelivery and writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under the prefix gateway/access/. Access is granted only through a statement in the bucket's resource-based policy, whose Principal is the role ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ApiGateLogDelivery. In the S3 console, open the bucket's Permissions tab and add a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-gateway-logs/gateway/access/*. Leave Block Public Access enabled, because the Principal names a single role and not a wildcard. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, this bucket policy allow is sufficient unless an explicit deny applies. In the ApiGate delivery settings, enter the bucket name, the prefix, and the role ARN. Use the Send test file action and confirm that a test object appears under the prefix. If delivery fails with AccessDenied, check the Resource element in the bucket policy for a mistyped prefix.

This guide covers a legacy TrafficLens collector that writes network flow logs to the bucket example-flow-logs using static credentials. The collector authenticates as the IAM user flowlogs-writer in account 444455556666. It uploads one object per ten-minute window under the prefix vpc-flow/daily/. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the user, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Attach a policy to flowlogs-writer that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/vpc-flow/daily/*. Do not add a Principal-based statement to the bucket policy for this user. Because the user and the bucket are in the same account, the identity-based allow takes effect without further bucket configuration. Store the access key in the collector's credential file with permissions 0600. Run the collector in dry-run mode, then verify that the first object appears under vpc-flow/daily/ within ten minutes.

This guide covers a legacy TrafficLens collector that writes network flow logs to the bucket example-flow-logs using static credentials. The collector authenticates as the IAM user flowlogs-writer in account 444455556666. It uploads one object per ten-minute window under the prefix vpc-flow/daily/. Access is granted only by a statement in the bucket's resource-based policy, whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::444455556666:user/flowlogs-writer. Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/vpc-flow/daily/*. Do not attach any permission policy to the user itself for this purpose. Because the user and the bucket are in the same account, the bucket policy allow takes effect without further identity configuration. Store the access key in the collector's credential file with permissions 0600. Run the collector in dry-run mode, then verify that the first object appears under vpc-flow/daily/ within ten minutes.

This guide sets up AuditStream to deliver audit event logs to the bucket example-audit-logs, where the bucket owner must be able to read every delivered object. AuditStream uses the IAM role AuditStreamWriter in account 777788889999 and uploads JSON-lines files under the prefix audit/events/. The grant is made only by an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Add an inline policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-logs/audit/events/* and uses a Condition with s3:x-amz-acl equal to bucket-owner-full-control. Configure AuditStream to send the bucket-owner-full-control canned ACL with each upload. Requests without that header are denied because the policy condition is not met. Do not create or modify any bucket policy statement for AuditStreamWriter. After saving, trigger a manual export and inspect the object's ACL to confirm that the bucket owner has full control. If uploads return AccessDenied, confirm that the delivery configuration sends the ACL header.

This guide gives a SIEM ingestion role read access to the log files that the PacketTrail service delivers into the bucket example-packet-logs. The role is IAM role SiemIngestReader in account 222233334444, and it polls the prefix packet/capture/ every minute. It lists new keys and downloads each object once. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Attach a policy that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-packet-logs with a s3:prefix condition of packet/capture/*. In the same policy, allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-packet-logs/packet/capture/*. Do not add any statement for this role to the bucket policy. Configure the ingestion job to assume SiemIngestReader and set its bucket and prefix. Validate by listing the prefix with the role's credentials and downloading one recent object.

This guide gives a SIEM ingestion role read access to the log files that the PacketTrail service delivers into the bucket example-packet-logs. The role is IAM role SiemIngestReader in account 222233334444, and it polls the prefix packet/capture/ every minute. It lists new keys and downloads each object once. Add a statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-packet-logs with a s3:prefix condition of packet/capture/*. In a second statement, allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-packet-logs/packet/capture/*. Do not attach any permission policy for this bucket to the role. Configure the ingestion job to assume SiemIngestReader and set its bucket and prefix. Validate by listing the prefix with the role's credentials and downloading one recent object.

This guide configures retention cleanup for the bucket example-dns-logs, into which the ResolverLog service delivers query logs. A scheduled job runs as IAM role LogRetentionJob in account 555566667777 and removes delivered files after they are processed. It operates only on the prefix dns/queries/. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. Create a policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-logs/dns/queries/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a s3:prefix condition for dns/queries/. Do not edit the bucket policy, and do not grant s3:DeleteObject outside the prefix. If versioning is enabled, note that deletes create delete markers unless s3:DeleteObjectVersion is also allowed. Run the job against a test object and confirm that it is removed from the prefix listing.

Do not attach a permission policy to the role, and do not grant s3:DeleteObject outside the prefix. This guide covers delivery of large database slow-query logs by the QueryScope service, which uploads files over 100 MB using multipart upload. The delivery identity is IAM role QueryScopeDelivery in account 888899990000, and the target is the bucket example-db-logs under the prefix slowlog/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Attach a policy that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-logs/slowlog/*. Also allow s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-logs so that the service can find stalled uploads. Do not add any statement for this role to the bucket policy. Configure the service with the role ARN, the bucket, and the prefix. Start a delivery of a 250 MB test file and confirm that the completed object appears. Check that no incomplete uploads remain after a forced interruption.

This guide limits a regional log shipper to one region's partition of the bucket example-edge-logs. The EdgeShip service runs in the eu-west region and writes CDN request logs as the IAM role EdgeShipEuWest in account 333344445555. Objects go under the prefix edge/eu-west/ and nowhere else. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not touched. Create a policy that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/eu-west/*. Add an explicit Deny statement in the same policy for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/us-east/*, to guard against accidental cross-region writes. Make no changes to the bucket policy. Set the shipper's destination to the bucket and the eu-west prefix. Send a test log and verify that it lands under edge/eu-west/. Confirm that a write attempt to the us-east prefix is rejected.

Add an explicit Deny statement in the same bucket policy for s3:PutObject by that Principal on arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/us-east/*, to guard against accidental cross-region writes. Attach no permission policy to the role. Set the shipper's destination to the bucket and the eu-west prefix. Send a test log and verify that it lands under edge/eu-west/. Confirm that a write attempt to the us-east prefix is rejected.

This guide enforces encrypted transport for log files delivered by the MeshTrace service to the bucket example-mesh-logs. MeshTrace writes service mesh traces as the IAM role MeshTraceDelivery in account 666677778888, under the prefix mesh/traces/. It also checks the bucket's region before the first upload. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Attach a policy that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-mesh-logs/mesh/traces/* with a Condition where aws:SecureTransport is true. In the same policy, allow s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-mesh-logs. Make no edits to the bucket policy. Configure MeshTrace to use the HTTPS endpoint only. Send a test trace file and confirm that it is stored. Verify that an HTTP request made with the role's credentials is denied.
